predecessors.note: 'the Sciri were subjects of Attila and provided potent infantry for him'; after Nedao (454) the kingdom of Edeko followed. The huns dossier (eu-06-a) calls the Sciri among Attila's Germanic vassals but does not list them as a successor.

successors.note: Hunimund page: after Bolia 'The Ostrogoths won, and gained control of territory of the Sciri and Quadi'. The surviving Sciri went with Odoacer to Italy (kingdom-of-odoacer) or with Onoulphus to Constantinople; no land passed to them.

correction.text: 'the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers': the Danube-Tisza interfluve of Hungary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 454-468: the Scirian kingdom. 'Edeko established a Scirian kingdom in the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers'. The page has no map, area or infobox; the shape is the three Hungarian counties between the two rivers (Pest, Bács-Kiskun, Csongrád, about 20,000 km2 in all), a reading of the page's sentence. The Danube-Tisza interfluve north of the Hungarian border (Slovak Danubian Lowland) and south of it (Bačka) are not drawn. The page also puts a second group of Sciri 'in the Roman empire in Scythia Minor and Lower Moesia south of the Lower Danube' (undated), which holds no territory of its own and is not drawn. Infobox area: none on the page. Reviewer (eu-06-x, 2026-10-24): 56 of this shape's 67 cells (about 14,200 km2) lie inside the kingdom-of-the-gepids keyframe kingdom-of-the-gepids_454 (454-472, the Cliopatria 510 shape carried back), so the Alföld is drawn twice for 454-468; the Sciri page places Edeko's kingdom here, so the gepids dossier should leave it out until 468. Seven cells of Pest county west of the Danube (about 1,800 km2) also lie inside ostrogoths_455 and outside the page's 'between the Middle Danube and the Tisza'.

region.text: 'the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers': the Danube-Tisza interfluve of Hungary

ledger.note: 454: Edeko founds a Scirian kingdom in the Alföld. After 'winning a major victory at the Battle of Nedao in AD 454', 'Edeko established a Scirian kingdom in the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers, which he ruled together with his sons Odoacer and Onoulphus'. The page gives no year for the kingdom; 454 is the Nedao year of the same passage, and the Nedao page has the Sciri on the Germanic side that broke Hunnic power.

region.text: 'the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers': the Danube-Tisza interfluve of Hungary

ledger.note: 468: the Sciri are crushed at Bolia and the Ostrogoths take their land. 'the Sciri met with crushing defeat near the Bolia river (468 A.D.)' (a passage quoted on the Bolia page); the Hunimund page: 'In 469, Hunimund and allied Sciri fought the Ostrogoths ... The Ostrogoths won, and gained control of territory of the Sciri and Quadi'; Odoacer page 'at the Battle of Bolia in 468' and 'about 469'. The pages differ by a year (468, 468/469, 469); 468 is the Bolia article's infobox date.

region.text: 'the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers': the Danube-Tisza interfluve of Hungary

ledger.note: 468: the Scirian kingdom ends. 'the battle marked the end of the Sciri as a separate people' (Bolia page); 'Odoacer led most of the surviving Sciri, in addition to many Heruli and Rugii, into Italy' and 'Odoacer's brother Onoulphus went to Constantinople with other Sciri' (Sciri page, undated). After Theodoric killed Odoacer on 15 March 493 the page ends: 'By this time the Sciri disappear from history.'

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: The Gepid-led Germanic coalition defeats the Huns under Ellac; 'Hunnic dominance in Central and Eastern Europe was broken' and the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Suebi and the others became independent by the early 460s.
wars.note: The Nedao page lists the Sciri among the Germanic side; the Sciri page has them 'winning a major victory'. No Scirian border moves in 454 beyond the founding.

wars.name: Battle of Bolia

zones.text: 'the Middle Alföld between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers': the Danube-Tisza interfluve of Hungary

wars.outcome: Ostrogothic victory 'achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; 'the battle marked the end of the Sciri as a separate people' and the Ostrogoths 'gained control of territory of the Sciri'.
wars.note: Date 468 on the Bolia page (468/469 on the Sciri page, 469 on the Hunimund page). The Sciri page: 'In AD 468/469 the Sciri made a surprise attack on the Ostrogoths', encouraged by Hunimund of the Suebi; Leo I backed the anti-Gothic coalition. Footnote 10 of the Bolia page records an argument that the Ostrogoths lost; not followed.

certainty.note: The page gives the kingdom's position only as 'between the Middle Danube and the Tisza rivers'; no boundary.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested through eu-06-a's counterparts_needing_dossiers ('Rugii, Heruli, Sciri and Danubian Suebi') and named in the eu-06 scope. Five pages opened. The page dates the kingdom only through Nedao (454) and Bolia (468 or 469); the founding event is therefore conf 2. Edeko is 'probably not a Scirian himself'. The Sciri who entered Italy under Odoacer (476-493) are soldiers of the kingdom-of-odoacer dossier, not territory here; the Scirian group settled on Roman land in Scythia Minor and Lower Moesia (undated) is not drawn. No capital is named. Cliopatria rows near the kingdom: Huns 106-425/Hunnic Empire 426-673 (shape of 443-454 covers Pannonia), Ostrogoths 455-499 (the successor). The ostrogoths dossier has no 468 event for Bolia or the Scirian land; a gap-filler should add the matching gain from sciri. Wikidata id unknown.
